analysis.headline: Stocks slipped Tuesday after a hotter-than-expected October CPI report (S&P 500 -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.74%, Dow -0.30%), and this morning futures point to a tech-led rebound, with Nasdaq-100 futures up about 1.5% early on, while the bond market is closed for Veterans Day.
analysis.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October and core prices 0.3%, both a tenth above the Dow Jones consensus, though cooler than September's 0.6% headline gain; the BLS published no year-over-year rate because October 2025 prices were never collected during the 2025 shutdown. Traders read the report as locking in a December Fed rate hike, and some now price a half-point move, since core at 0.3% meets the bar Fed Governor Waller set for weighing a 50-basis-point hike (Stock Titan, investingLive). That sent the 2-year Treasury yield up about 18 basis points to roughly 4.73% and the 10-year up about 10 basis points to near 4.98%, briefly above 5%. Higher yields and a firmer dollar knocked gold futures down about 2% to settle near $4,030 and pushed Bitcoin to about $73,800, near a three-month low, while Brent crude eased 1.2% to $91.49, briefly dipping under $90 for the first time since August as President Trump said the Iran war could end soon. Nvidia's 5.5% drop made tech the weakest sector, but CoreWeave's raised 2026 revenue forecast is lifting tech futures this morning (MLQ.ai).
drivers: October CPI: +0.4% headline and +0.3% core month over month, vs. 0.3% and 0.2% expected, raising odds of a December Fed hike (BLS, CNBC).
Treasury selloff: the 2-year yield jumped about 18 basis points and the 10-year briefly topped 5% (investingLive).
Nvidia fell about 5.5% and dragged the Nasdaq, as tech was the S&P 500's weakest sector (TradingKey).
Gold fell about 2% and Bitcoin slid toward a three-month low on higher yields and a stronger dollar, while Brent eased on hopes the Iran war could end (Mining.com, Closing Look).
watch: Today (Wed): Veterans Day, so U.S. stock markets are open but the bond market and the Fed are closed (investingLive).

Thu Nov 12: weekly jobless claims (forecast near 195,000 after 189,000), Cisco and Applied Materials earnings after the close, and Fed speakers including Hammack, Barr, Goolsbee, Daly, Schmid and Williams (Yahoo Finance, MLQ.ai).
Fri Nov 13, 8:30 a.m. ET: October producer price index, expected +0.4% headline and +0.3% core, plus Fed speakers Collins, Bowman, Daly and Jefferson (Yahoo Finance).

helium.headline: North American Helium's new Stewart Valley plant, officially opened Oct. 15 as Canada's largest helium purification facility, is ramping up just as Ottawa moves to give helium oil-and-gas-style tax treatment and helium prices run hot.
helium.summary: NAH said its Stewart Valley purification plant in southwest Saskatchewan came onstream on Sept. 20, 2026, producing about 73 million cubic feet of helium a year from a field Ryder Scott credits with 1.1 billion cubic feet of reserves, and the province says it will lift Saskatchewan's helium output by more than 40%. The project went from discovery well to production in 13 months, and local news reports a possible $100 million helium liquefier in Swift Current, which the company says is not finalized. The 2026 federal budget proposes treating helium exploration and development costs like conventional oil and gas for expenses from Nov. 5, 2026 (Prince Albert Daily Herald, Nov. 7). In the U.S. market NAH sells into, the Department of Energy named helium a critical material on Oct. 23, and law firm Mintz says spot helium prices have nearly tripled since March 2026.

realestate.headline: Portland-area home prices are holding roughly flat, with RMLS data showing an October metro median of $545,000 (up 0.9% from a year ago), while new listings shrink and mortgage rates sit just above 7%.
realestate.summary: RMLS figures summarized by RE/MAX put the Portland metro median sale price at $545,000 in October, up 0.9% from October 2025, and the year-to-date median at $549,000, down 0.2%; homes took 67 days of total market time, two fewer than a year ago, and new listings fell about 12% year over year. Redfin's city-only measure is softer, with a $518,000 median for the three months ending September, down 2.2% from a year earlier, and Realtor.com data on FRED shows a metro median listing price of $580,000 in October. Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate eased for a third straight week to 7.18% on Nov. 5, still well above 6.22% a year ago. On rents, CBRE says the average Portland apartment rent was about $1,764 at the end of the third quarter, up roughly 0.7% from the prior quarter, with occupancy near 95%; none of these sources broke out North Portland, St. Johns or Sauvie Island.
